units.source: Meeting transcription
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting transcription is in beta__TRILIUM_PH_1__

Meeting transcription is a new feature and is still in beta. It has not been tested on every operating system, audio setup and meeting application, so it might fail to capture the audio, miss part of a meeting or behave differently from what this page describes. Before relying on it for an important meeting, try it on a short call first.

If something does not work, please __TRILIUM_PH_0__report the issue__TRILIUM_PH_1__, mentioning your operating system and the meeting application you used. The __TRILIUM_PH_2__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ option described below keeps what is needed to reproduce a problem.

Meeting transcription turns a meeting into text while it happens: Trilium listens to your microphone and to what the other participants say through your speakers, and writes down who said what in a new note. Recognition runs entirely on your device, so no audio leaves it (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below).
Meeting transcription is available only in the desktop application. It is not available when Trilium is accessed through a browser, nor in the mobile application.
Enabling meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Meeting transcription is off by default. To turn it on, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and turn on __TRILIUM_PH_4__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_5__. This adds the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_8__ button to the __TRILIUM_PH_9__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_10__, marked with a __TRILIUM_PH_11__Beta__TRILIUM_PH_12__ badge.

The speech recognition models are not part of Trilium. The first time you transcribe a meeting, Trilium asks to download them; see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Downloaded resources__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for the sizes and how to manage them. Each device downloads its own copy.
Transcribing a meeting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
If the models are not downloaded yet, confirm the download and wait for it to finish.

Trilium creates a text note titled with the current date and time (for example __TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting 2026-10-15 14:30__TRILIUM_PH_1__) in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note Inbox__TRILIUM_PH_3__, opens it and starts transcribing. While it transcribes, the button turns into a __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Stop transcribing__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button and shows the time elapsed. Beside it, a reminder asks you to let everyone in the meeting know that it is being transcribed and to ask for their consent; it closes by itself after 10 seconds, or when you click it.
To end the transcription, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Stop transcribing__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. Trilium finishes transcribing what was already said before it stops.

Only one meeting can be transcribed at a time. The note itself is an ordinary text note: you can take notes in it during the meeting, rename it or move it anywhere in the tree. It carries the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label.

Trilium tells you when your microphone or the meeting's audio is not being transcribed. It shows a message saying which one and why, the time on the button turns red and the button's tooltip says that some audio is not being transcribed:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Not captured__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the transcription started without that audio, for example because there is no microphone or because Trilium was not allowed to record the screen and its audio. Connect the microphone or allow the recording, then stop the transcription and start it again.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_1__: nothing has arrived from it for 10 seconds, as when its capture hangs. Stop the transcription and start it again; what was transcribed until then is kept.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_1__: it has delivered nothing but silence, for 15 seconds from your microphone or for a minute from the meeting. A microphone muted in your system's settings, or with a mute button of its own, does this. A meeting nobody speaks in for a minute does it too, so this message can be ignored when the others are just quiet.
Each message shows once. __TRILIUM_PH_0__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_3__ clear by themselves once sound arrives again.

If the transcription stops on its own, for example because the audio could no longer be captured, Trilium shows a message and keeps everything transcribed until then. Closing Trilium during a meeting waits for the transcription to finish first.
The transcript__TRILIUM_PH_0__

The transcript is stored as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__attachment__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the meeting note and is shown in a collapsible __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section above the note's content. It updates as the meeting goes on, one paragraph per speaker turn, each with the time it started. While the meeting is being transcribed, the header of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_5__ section shows the level of your microphone (__TRILIUM_PH_6__Me__TRILIUM_PH_7__) and of the meeting's audio (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Others__TRILIUM_PH_9__), so you can tell that both are being heard, even while the section is collapsed; a source that is not being transcribed is marked __TRILIUM_PH_10__Not captured__TRILIUM_PH_11__, __TRILIUM_PH_12__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_13__ or __TRILIUM_PH_14__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_15__. While someone is talking, __TRILIUM_PH_16__Speaking…__TRILIUM_PH_17__ shows under their name until their words are transcribed. If you are reading the end of the transcript, it scrolls to follow new text.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section is expanded each time the note is opened. To collapse it, click its header; it stays collapsed only until the note is opened again.

The transcript is also listed among the note's attachments, under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Generated by Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Opening it from there shows the same view of the transcript. Deleting the attachment deletes the transcript, and the section disappears from the note.
What you say into your microphone is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Me__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

What the other participants say is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Speaker 1__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Speaker 2__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and so on, while __TRILIUM_PH_4__Identify speakers__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is on; otherwise it is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_6__Others__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

To name a speaker, click their name, type the new name and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The name changes on every turn of that speaker. Press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to cancel, or clear the name to restore the default one.

To show the transcript with or without hesitations such as "uh", "um" and stuttered words, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Hide filler words__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button above it, which shows as pressed while they are hidden. While they are shown, they are grayed out, so you can see what hiding them would remove. This affects only what is shown; the stored transcript keeps every word.

To copy the transcript as plain text, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Copy transcript__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button above it. Each turn is copied with the speaker's name and the time it started, as shown, so the copy leaves out filler words while they are hidden.

If the meeting note is __TRILIUM_PH_0__protected__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and the protected session is locked during the meeting, the transcript cannot be saved. Trilium keeps it in memory and saves it once you enter the protected session again, as long as Trilium stays open.
Configuration__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The settings are in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__, and are shown once __TRILIUM_PH_4__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is on.
Option
Description
__TRILIUM_PH_0__European languages__TRILIUM_PH_1__

The speech recognition model. Both are versions of NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 model and recognize 25 European languages and work out which one is spoken. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Standard__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a smaller download and runs well on most computers. __TRILIUM_PH_2__High accuracy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ makes fewer mistakes, but is a larger download and needs about 1.6 GB more memory while transcribing. A model is downloaded the first time you transcribe with it.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Identify speakers__TRILIUM_PH_1__

Tells the other participants apart and labels each of them separately, using the TitaNet model. Voices are compared only during the meeting: nothing about a voice is stored, and no one is recognized from one meeting to the next. Turn it off if it mixes up voices. The change applies from the next meeting.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_1__

Keeps the audio of the meeting, the settings used and the transcript as it was produced, so that a problem can be reported and reproduced. It takes about 230 MB per hour of meeting and is never deleted automatically. The folder where they are kept is shown below the option.

Before turning on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_1__, ask everyone in the meeting to agree to being recorded. In several countries and US states, recording a conversation without everyone's consent is a criminal offense. The audio is stored unencrypted, even for protected notes. While the option is on, the tooltip of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button says so, and the reminder shown when the transcription starts mentions that the audio is kept.
The sizes and licenses of the models are listed in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Downloaded resources__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Meeting transcription does not use any online service:
The audio is recognized on your device by the open-source sherpa-onnx engine. Trilium does not send the audio or the transcript to any online service, and no account or API key is needed.
An Internet connection is needed only to download the models, from Hugging Face and from the sherpa-onnx project on GitHub. Once they are downloaded, meeting transcription works offline.
Speaker identification compares voices only during the meeting. Nothing about a voice is stored.
The audio is not kept, unless __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is on. Those recordings stay in a folder on your device and are never synchronized.

The transcript itself is an attachment of the meeting note, so it is handled like the rest of your notes. If you use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it is synchronized to your sync server and your other devices. To keep it encrypted, transcribe into a __TRILIUM_PH_2__protected__TRILIUM_PH_3__ note: the transcript of a protected note is protected too.
Limitations__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Meeting transcription needs a speech recognition engine that does not load on every computer, for example on Linux distributions older than Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. Where it does not load, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button does not appear, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__ options say so, and the log records why.

The transcript is made from the audio played by your device. A participant whose voice does not come out of your speakers or headphones, for example someone in the same room, is transcribed only as far as your microphone picks them up, and is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Me__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Speaker identification works best with a few clearly distinct voices. Similar voices, many participants or poor call quality can lead to speakers being merged or split.
Accuracy is lower for languages other than English, and the model can switch to the wrong language for short passages.
Transcribing uses a noticeable amount of processor time and memory, especially with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__High accuracy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ model.
